items.explain: x is [1 3 5 7 9]; end is the last index (5), so end-1 picks the fourth element, 7.
.* multiplies element by element, so B(2,1) = 3 * 3 = 9; A * A would have given 15.
max returns the largest value (8) and its position; 8 is the second element, so i = 2.
The range includes both ends, 0 and 1, with 0.1 steps: that is 11 points.

options: A red solid line with markers
items.explain: In the line-spec string, r is the colour red and -- is the dashed line style.
The apostrophe transposes the 1x3 row vector into a 3x1 column vector.

items.q: A Simulink model connects a Constant block (value 2) to an Integrator block (initial condition 0) and then to a Scope. The simulation runs for 5 s. What does the Scope show at t = 5 s?
items.explain: The integrator outputs the running integral of its input: 2 * 5 = 10, a straight ramp from 0 to 10.

items.q: A Sine Wave block with amplitude 3 feeds a Saturation block with limits -1 and +1, then a Scope. What does the Scope show?
options: A sine clipped flat at +1 and -1
items.explain: Saturation passes the signal unchanged inside the limits and holds it at the limit outside, so the peaks are cut flat.

items.q: Step block (step time 1 s, final value 1) -> Gain block (gain 4) -> Integrator (initial condition 0) -> Scope. What is the Scope value at t = 3 s?
items.explain: The integrator input is 4 only from t = 1 s onward, so at t = 3 s the integral is 4 * (3 - 1) = 8.

items.q: You need to generate C code from a Simulink model for a microcontroller. Which solver setting must the model use?
options: Any solver with zero-crossing detection on
items.explain: Embedded targets run at a constant sample rate, so code generation needs a fixed-step solver; variable-step solvers change the step size at run time.

items.q:
What happens when this script runs in a fresh workspace?

for i = 1:5
  s = s + i;
end
disp(s)
options: Error because s is not defined before the loop
items.explain: MATLAB does not assume a starting value; s must be initialised (s = 0;) before you add to it.
